Question: Can we shoot the nuclear waste into Interstellar space to safely get rid of it from the Earth?

Question: Why wasn’t the small populated and defencless Scandinavia conquered by the Holy Roman Empire and later the German empire?
Answer: Because until WWII, it was a logistical impossibility to support a foreign army in Scandinavia. This is what Scandinavia mostly looks like. There’s a reason why the population is small. There’s nothing to eat. The land you’re seeing here has an inch or two of topsoil, except the areas with no trees, which are bogs. In most places, rocks poke out of the soil, from small ones you can hold in your hand to large boulders that you’ll need several teams of oxen to shift. Patches of the ground look green, because moss is green and can grow directly on rocks without any soil. Up until WWII, armies were heavily into supporting themselves off the land. You need serious forest skills to support yourself off this land, and if you bring an entire army, it’s simply not doable. If you have to ship all supplies from Germany, they’ll spoil before they are halfway. You can’t get an army and its supplies here until you’ve invented the internal combustion engine. And once the army is here – good luck finding an enemy to fight.
